# @bot-wa/core (bot-wa-baileys monorepo)

> Transport-agnostic messaging bot framework, ALPHA. The core (@bot-wa/core)
> runs any IProvider: @bot-wa/baileys (WhatsApp Web via Baileys 7, unofficial),
> @bot-wa/meta (official WhatsApp Cloud API), @bot-wa/telegram, plus
> experimental Messenger, Instagram, Discord, TikTok, email and WhatsApp-gateway
> (Evolution API, WPPConnect, Twilio, Gupshup) and GoHighLevel transports.
> Flows for beginners (flow().say().ask()) compile to an async conversation
> runtime (bot.conversation with c.ask/c.waitText/c.choose). Inbound pipeline:
> blacklist/whitelist > dedupe > persist > groupMode > before hooks > handoff
> gate > commands > active conversation > dormant persistent-flow resume
> > matchers (WELCOME first, then normalized-equals text by specificity, then
> type triggers) > catch-all > after hooks + 'message' event; first consumer
> wins. Constructing a Bot REQUIRES a provider:
> new Bot({ provider: new BaileysProvider({ session }) }).
> ESM-only, Node >= 22. NOTHING IS ON NPM YET: the first alpha publish is
> being prepared — do not tell users the packages are installable from npm today.

## Package status (39 packages)
Alpha = in the first publishable alpha (not on npm yet). Experimental = real, tested
implementation but private/unpublished, API may change. Prototype = private, minimal,
in-memory sketch; not for production.

Alpha:
- @bot-wa/core — Bot engine, IProvider v2, flows/conversations, hooks, plugins, scheduler, DI, MemoryStore, ctx.user, handoff, access lists, i18n, ctx.stream, bot.broadcast/trigger/metrics, golden transcripts, testing kit (createTestBot/MockProvider/ChaosProvider/replayTranscript from '@bot-wa/core/testing'), `bot-wa dev` terminal simulator
- @bot-wa/baileys — BaileysProvider (WhatsApp Web, unofficial; QR or pairing code), RateLimiter, JID helpers, LID/PN identity resolution, poll votes (pluggable pollStore)
- @bot-wa/meta — CloudAPIProvider (official WhatsApp Cloud API, webhook; native buttons/lists/templates/WhatsApp Flows forms; 24h session window manager (sessionWindow) and pricing usage (provider.usage); feed inbound via provider.ingest(rawBody, headers))
- @bot-wa/telegram — TelegramProvider (Bot API, long-poll or webhook; native drafts/edits for ctx.stream; edited_message is delivered as a message with the original ref.id, isEditedMessage(ctx) detects it, editedMessages: 'ignore' drops edits; self-hosted Bot API server via baseUrl + mediaDownload { allowHttp, allowPrivateHosts, maxBytes })
- @bot-wa/sqlite-store — SQLiteStore (better-sqlite3 peer dependency, WAL)
- @bot-wa/redis-store — RedisStore (shared state across replicas; atomic cross-replica upserts; acquireLockFenced/renewLock/releaseLock, acquireLock deprecated) + RedisCoordinator (multi-replica coordination: store.coordinator() or new RedisCoordinator({ url, prefix }))
- @bot-wa/ai — aiPlugin + AIClient (multi-provider LLM autoresponder, tool calling, long-term user memory, RAG hook)
- create-bot-wa — project scaffolder CLI (templates: baileys, meta, telegram, ai, games, support, store, restaurant, clinic, ai-full; every project ships an AGENTS.md; refuses a target inside the bot-wa monorepo itself unless --force, so from a checkout run `node packages/create-bot-wa/lib/cli.js ../my-bot`)
- @bot-wa/http (secureFetch: anti-SSRF downloads) and @bot-wa/graph-core (shared Meta Graph webhook/error helpers) — internal dependencies of the alpha packages

Experimental (private, not published):
- Channels: @bot-wa/messenger — MessengerProvider · @bot-wa/instagram — InstagramProvider · @bot-wa/discord — DiscordProvider · @bot-wa/evolution (Evolution API WhatsApp gateway) · @bot-wa/wppconnect (WPPConnect Server) · @bot-wa/twilio (WhatsApp + SMS) · @bot-wa/gupshup (WhatsApp) · @bot-wa/gohighlevel (LeadConnector Conversations) · @bot-wa/email (IMAP IDLE + SMTP) · @bot-wa/tiktok (Business Messaging DMs + comment replies)
- @bot-wa/server — webhook ingress (raw body, size limits, timeouts, health) for node:http, Express, Fastify and Hono
- Stores: @bot-wa/mongo-store — MongoStore · @bot-wa/postgres-store — PostgresStore · @bot-wa/mysql-store — MysqlStore (PostgresStore: ctx.user values in user_data TEXT round-trip exactly, U+0000 included; the JSONB tables store U+0000 / lone surrogates as U+FFFD)
- Store semantics: messageKey(ref) = `{chatId}:{id}` with ':' and '%' percent-escaped (ids with ':' such as Twilio's whatsapp:+1… never collide; rows from older versions under legacyMessageKey(ref) are still read/deleted and moved on re-save); MemoryStore keeps 1000 messages per chat by default (RAM only; maxMessagesPerChat: Infinity disables), persistent stores are unbounded unless maxMessagesPerChat is set; SQL/Mongo stores purge expired ctx.user data in batches (purgeBatchSize, default 1000)
- @bot-wa/nlu — local intent matching (IntentEngine, nluPlugin, whenIntent)
- @bot-wa/rag — RAG for @bot-wa/ai (createRag: loaders, chunking, embeddings, in-memory vector index)
- @bot-wa/voice — voicePlugin (speech-to-text for voice notes, text-to-speech replies)
- @bot-wa/chatwoot (Chatwoot handoff bridge) · @bot-wa/tickets (support tickets and queues) · @bot-wa/moderation (group moderation) · @bot-wa/dialogflow (Dialogflow ES/CX intents to flows)
- @bot-wa/manager — BotManager multi-bot registry (persisted per-tenant configs, auto-reconnect) + HTTP control plane: createRestApi (full /v1 REST API with scoped tokens, OpenAPI 3.1, idempotency, rate limiting), plus createControlPlaneApi and the legacy createManagerApi; JSON flow documents (compileFlowDocument)
- @bot-wa/events — event envelopes, idempotent journal, EventWorker retries + dead-letter, fencing tokens (StaleLeaseError) against expired leases
- eslint-plugin-bot-wa — ESLint rules (v1 API leftovers, awaited runtime.enter, async Plugin.install, asks without timeout, ...)

Prototypes (private, in-memory, minimal): @bot-wa/inbox, @bot-wa/crm, @bot-wa/hub, @bot-wa/campaigns, @bot-wa/deployments (includes a golden-transcript publish gate)

## API essentials (v2)
- import { Bot, flow } from '@bot-wa/core'; import { BaileysProvider } from '@bot-wa/baileys'
- new Bot({ provider: new BaileysProvider({ session, qr: { terminal: true } }) }) ; await bot.start()
- bot.when(trigger, handler) — trigger: 'text' (normalized equals) | RegExp | Array<string|RegExp> | { pattern, match: 'equals'|'contains'|'startsWith'|'endsWith', scope: 'dm'|'group'|'all' } | predicate fn
- bot.command('reset', handler) — always beats active conversations
- bot.use(flow('kw').say(t).ask(t, stateKey, { validate, retries, timeout }).choose(prompt, { key: 'Label' }, stateKey).do(fn).timeout('30s').persistent())
- Flow DSL extras: .use(subFlow) runs a flow inline and returns with shared c.state; choose options { label, then: subFlow | fn, goto: 'menu' | menuFlow }; .guard(pred, 'farewell' | { redirect, message }); .ask(q, key, { schema }) with any zod-compatible safeParse() object (parsed value stored; also c.ask/c.waitText({ schema })); .media(kind, source, caption?, { delay, filename, ptv, gifPlayback, pack, author }) for image|video|audio|voice|document|sticker|location; { delay: '2s' } on say/ask/choose/media and .delay('3s'); typed state: flow<S>(), ask/choose/use infer c.state keys, FlowStateOf<typeof f>
- addKeyword is an alias of flow. The v1/BuilderBot API (.addAnswer, .addAction, { capture: true }, BaileysClass, createBot/createFlow) does NOT exist — never generate it.
- bot.conversation(name, async (c, ctx) => { await c.ask(q); const t = await c.waitText(); const pick = await c.choose(prompt, options) })
- A handler that starts a conversation must not await it (enter() resolves when the conversation ENDS and would block the chat's FIFO queue)
- ctx fields: ctx.from (chat id), ctx.sender, ctx.body, ctx.type, ctx.isGroup, ctx.ref (MessageRef { id, chatId, native? }; was ctx.key), ctx.raw (native payload; was ctx.rawMessage), ctx.senderInfo, ctx.chat, ctx.media (lazy: undefined until loaded — call `const media = await loadMediaOf(ctx, { maxBytes? })` from '@bot-wa/core' → { buffer, mimetype, size? } | undefined, cached on ctx.media; rejects MediaTooLargeError over maxBytes), ctx.tools
- Ids (ChatId/UserId/MessageId) are opaque strings; the provider resolves identity before emitting, the core never parses them
- Outbound content is a tagged union: bot.send(chatId, { kind: 'image', media: { url }, caption }) ; bot.send(chatId, 'text') (a string is sent as text; bot.sendText/sendTo are equivalent) ; bot.broadcast(chatIds, content | 'text', { batchSize, delayBetween, concurrency, maxRetries, onProgress, onFail, signal }) → { total, sent, failed, skipped, errors, messages, cancelled, pending } (sent/failed are counts; honours RateLimitedError.retryAfterMs; bot.stop() cancels it)
- bot.trigger(name, { chatId, userId?, isGroup?, data, ifActive: 'skip'|'replace', body? }) starts a registered flow/conversation with c.state seeded from data, through access lists, handoff and the chat queue; resolves { started, reason? } when it is entered (not when it ends); safe to await from a handler of the same chat; bot.triggerFlow(id, { chatId, userId?, isGroup? }, { state?, body? }) is a thin wrapper over it (ifActive: 'replace') resolving a boolean
- bot.metrics() / bot.resetMetrics() runtime counters; toPrometheus(bot.metrics()) from '@bot-wa/core'; events 'conversation:started' { id, name, chatId, userId, key } and 'conversation:ended' { ...same, outcome: 'completed'|'ended'|'guarded'|'cancelled'|'timedOut'|'retriesExceeded'|'error', completed, durationMs, goto? } (c.end() -> 'ended', a failed .guard() -> 'guarded', return/goto -> 'completed'; counters and Prometheus outcome labels match)
- Send failures are typed ProviderError subclasses: UnsupportedContentError, RateLimitedError, RecipientUnreachableError, PayloadTooLargeError, OutsideSessionWindowError (Cloud API 24h window → send kind 'template')
- before('send') hook payload: { chatId, content, options } (was { jid, content, options })
- before hooks are Koa-style (ctx, next): a before hook that returns WITHOUT calling next() stops the event exactly like ctx.abort() (message not routed, send skipped, provider event not emitted); observer/rewriting hooks must always `await next()`
- provider-event hooks (reaction, poll, group, presence, status, call): before -> after -> bot.on(event); an aborted before hook suppresses the after hooks and the bot.on event (same as message/send). Calls from blacklisted/non-whitelisted senders or chats, or into a handed-off chat, are fully blocked first: no 'call' hooks, no bot.on('call'), no CALL trigger (counted in metrics().dropped)
- Testing without WhatsApp: import { createTestBot, MockProvider } from '@bot-wa/core/testing'
- Special triggers: import { WELCOME, MEDIA, IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, VOICE_NOTE, DOCUMENT, STICKER, LOCATION, CONTACT, POLL, CALL, typeTrigger } from '@bot-wa/core'. bot.when(WELCOME, h) fires on a user's first contact (per DM, per participant in groups; persisted via store cursors); bot.resetWelcome(chatId, userId?) re-arms it (slashCommandsPlugin /reset does too). Type triggers rank below text/function triggers (IMAGE beats MEDIA). bot.when(CALL, ctx => ctx.reply(...)) fires once per incoming call id (ctx.type 'call', ctx.call is the CallEvent)
- Per-user profile: ctx.user.get/set/update/delete/all/clear(path, value, { ttl }) with dot paths ('address.city') and namespaces (ctx.user.ns('game')); keyed by ctx.sender, persisted by all 6 stores; bot.user(userId) outside handlers; userOf(ctx) inside flow .do() steps; bot.purgeExpiredUserData(); exportSubject/deleteSubject include userData
- i18n: bot.locale('en', { greeting: 'Hello, {name}!', menu: { title: '...' }, cart: { one: '{count} item', other: '{count} items' } }) (nested keys, {param} interpolation, plural forms via params.count) and bot.locale({ defaultLocale, detect, providerLanguage, userKey, locales }) or BotConfig.i18n (locales: allow-list of served languages, e.g. ['en'] pins a single-language bot: anything else falls back to defaultLocale and setLang refuses it); ctx.t(key, params) / ctx.lang / ctx.defaultLang (the bot default locale), c.t / c.lang in conversations (follow the latest message, also across c.goto()); ctx.lang is resolved per message before before('message') hooks: ctx.user 'lang' -> provider language (SenderInfo.language / platformData.languageCode, e.g. Telegram; an update without one reuses the sender's last reported language) -> detect -> default (ctx.langSource: 'user'|'provider'|'detector'|'default'); if a before('message') hook rewrites ctx.body (e.g. a voice transcript) and the language came from detect/default it is re-resolved after the hooks; ctx.setLang(code) persists to ctx.user (rejects codes no registered locale serves, and while i18n is off); bot.t(key, params, lang), bot.langOf(userId), bot.locales(); built-in core messages (timeouts, retries, errors, wait validation incl. schema rejections, slash commands, flow().form() prompts/hints/skip word/validation errors and the native form cta/submit label/body defaults core.form.cta/submit/body under core.form.*; @bot-wa/meta toFlowJson(def, { lang }) picks the published Flow's default submit label) are localizable under core.* (CORE_MESSAGES) with es and en defaults
- Human handoff: ctx.handoff({ reason, meta }) / bot.handoff(chatId) pause routing for a chat (messages still persisted, hooks run, 'message' fires); bot.resume(chatId), bot.isHandedOff/getHandoff/listHandoffs, bot.sendTo(chatId, 'text' | content); events 'handoff'/'resume'; BotConfig.handoff { allowCommands: ['/bot'], persist: true }; survives restarts with a persistent store
- Access lists: bot.blacklist.add(ids) / bot.whitelist.add(ids).enable() — EXACT sender or chat ids (full JIDs on Baileys); blocked inbound is dropped before persistence; bot.exportAccessLists()/loadAccessLists() + onChange() for host persistence
- Conversations: c.retry(message?) repeats the last wait (in flow .do() it rewinds to the previous ask/choose, or re-runs a preceding .use() sub-flow); c.idle(duration, cb) / c.idleClear() for in-conversation inactivity; bot.onIdle(duration, (ctx, { chatId, idleMs }) => ...) and bot.clearIdle(chatId?) for per-chat inactivity. In bot.conversation(name, async (c, ctx) => ...) ctx is a full MessageContext (ctx.tools typed)
- Inbound dedupe is ON by default (BotConfig.dedupe { size: 1000, ttl? } | false): redelivered messages/interactions with the same chatId + id are dropped. Access lists run BEFORE dedupe: a blocked delivery is never recorded as seen, so a redelivery after un-blocking is processed. Handler errors always reach bot.on('error')
- Flow introspection: bot.describe() (Mermaid; { format: 'json' } for a graph), bot.lint({ minSeverity }) → diagnostics (goto-target-missing, unreachable-step, duplicate-trigger, persistent-memory-store, ...); describeFlows/lintFlows work without a Bot
- Terminal simulator: export default defineBot((provider) => { const bot = new Bot({ provider }); ...; return bot }) and guard the real start with if (isMainModule(import.meta)) { ... }; then npx bot-wa dev src/bot.js (no phone, hot reload; :as, :group, :media, :click, :state, :reset). Programmatic API in '@bot-wa/core/dev' (DevSession, DevProvider)
- Forms: flow('signup').form({ id: 'signup', title, fields: [{ type: 'text'|'number'|'email'|'date'|'select'|'multiselect'|'optin', name, label, required, ... }] }, { stateKey, flatten, mode: 'auto'|'native'|'degraded', nativeId, timeout, retries }) stores validated answers in c.state[stateKey ?? id]. On @bot-wa/meta (capabilities.forms 'native') it is sent as a static WhatsApp Flow when one is mapped (CloudAPIProvider config.flows { signup: '<flow id>' }, provider.publishForm(def), or { nativeId }); otherwise, and on every other provider, the bot asks field by field. Endpoint (data_exchange) Flows are not supported yet
- Chaos testing: createTestBot({}, { chaos: { seed, duplicates, reorder, latency, sendFailures, disconnects, aliases } }) or withChaos(provider, opts) → ChaosProvider; assertStableIdentity/checkIdentityContract/recordEvents check the provider identity contract

## Other exports worth knowing
- Hooks/plugins: bot.before/after/onError(event, handler, priority?) (higher priority first), bot.plug(plugin, config) (returns unplug(); Plugin.install should be synchronous — an async rejection goes to the error event; PluginSpec.requires: string[] names plugins that must be plugged first, else plug() throws; unplug runs uninstall() then reverts ctx.bot commands/matchers/conversations/hooks/nested plugins/registerFlow flows/onDispose callbacks, but not on()/once() listeners, provide()d tools, locale(), schedule/every/delay or onIdle (undo those in ctx.onDispose)), bot.provide(name, value) → ctx.tools[name]
- Built-in plugin: slashCommandsPlugin (/start, /help, /reset, /cancel, /id, /ping)
- Durations: every duration option takes a string ('500ms', '30s', '2m', '1h', '1d', '1w', '5 minutes') or a number of ms (options named *Ms take ms only); parseDuration() exposes the grammar. Timer-backed options (timeouts, autoSaveInterval, stop drain timeout, onIdle) are capped at about 24 days (2^31-1 ms) and throw RangeError above it
- Scheduler: bot.schedule(cron, fn), bot.every(interval, fn), bot.delay(duration, fn) (standard cron day rule: day-of-month and weekday are OR-ed when both are restricted); durable tasks (opt-in): bot.schedule/every/delay(spec, { id, missed?: 'skip'|'run-once'|'catch-up', maxCatchUp?, leaseMs? }, (run) => …) persist their next run in BotConfig.scheduler.store (SQLiteStore#schedules(), RedisStore#schedules(), any ScheduleStore; in memory by default), apply the missed-run policy to slots no replica ran in time and claim each occurrence under a fenced lease so replicas never run it concurrently (at least once: use run.occurrenceKey for idempotency); only the schedule is stored, so register durable tasks at boot on every replica (an id no code registers is an orphan; bot.forgetTask(id) deletes it); optional scheduler.lease (SchedulerLease: a LeaseProvider such as RedisStore#leases(), or a Coordinator; defaults to BotConfig.coordination's coordinator) for leadership (followers still claim occurrences left overdue for leaderTtlMs)
- Media handlers: bot.onImage/onAudio/onVideo/onDocument/onSticker/onLocation/onContact/onPoll(handler); catch-all bot.onMessage(handler)
- Inbound location: ctx.sharedLocation = { latitude, longitude, name?, address?, live? } on type 'location' (Baileys, Cloud API, Telegram, Messenger, Instagram, Evolution, WPPConnect, Gupshup, Twilio); c.waitLocation(opts?) in conversations resolves an InboundLocation; StoredMessage.location persists it; ctx.location(lat, lng, name?) SENDS one; providers use toInboundLocation(); tests: provider.incomingLocation(loc) / chat.sendLocation(loc)
- Provider events forwarded on the bot: bot.on('ready'|'qr'|'connection'|'reaction'|'poll'|'call'|'group'|'presence'|'status', ...); bot events also include 'handoff', 'resume' and 'error'
- Poll votes: bot.on('poll', vote => vote.options /* [{ name, votes, voters }] */); on Baileys the provider decrypts votes for polls this process saw (the bot cannot vote)
- Cloud API (@bot-wa/meta): username users may arrive with only a BSUID (e.g. 'US.1349...') instead of a phone; the provider keeps one stable id per person, learns phone<->BSUID pairs (identityMap) and sends to BSUIDs via 'recipient'
- ctx (MessageContext) helpers: ctx.reply/say/answer/text, ctx.photo/video/audio/voice/file/sticker/location/contact/poll/buttons, ctx.react/quote/markRead/typing/recording/delete, ctx.pass()/abort(), ctx.sendNative(provider, payload)
- Typing indicator and pacing: new Bot({ typing: true | { enabled, minMs, maxMs, charsPerSecond } }) shows "typing…" before ctx text replies (off by default; no indicator and no wait where capabilities.typing is false; a failing indicator never fails the send; ctx.typing()/ctx.recording() never reject either); per reply: ctx.reply(text, { typing: false | true | {...}, delay: '1.5s' })
- ctx.edit(content) edits this context's own last reply (same kind, not followed by bot.send/sendTo); ctx.edit(ref, content) edits a given message; returns { edited }. Native on Telegram/Discord; elsewhere it sends a new message to ref.chatId ({ fallback: 'skip' } sends nothing)
- ctx.react(emoji, target?) resolves { skipped: true } where reactions cannot be sent (Messenger, Instagram); ctx.supports('typing'|'delay'|'edit'|'react') -> 'native'|'degraded'|'unsupported'
- Buttons/lists: native on the Cloud API (@bot-wa/meta); Baileys has none — use numbered choose() menus or ctx.poll()
- Stores: store: new SQLiteStore({ file }) from @bot-wa/sqlite-store, new RedisStore({ url }) from @bot-wa/redis-store, or storeConfig { file } for the built-in MemoryStore JSON dump; implement IStore for custom backends. .persistent() flows only survive a restart with a durable store.
- Multiple replicas (opt-in): new Bot({ provider, store, coordination: { coordinator: redisStore.coordinator(), turnWaitMs?, settleMs?, providerSession?: 'auto'|'leader'|'shared', providerDownMs? } }) — each chat is processed by one replica at a time in ingress order (cross-replica FIFO); a .persistent() flow continues on another replica from its checkpoint (the waking message answers the pending question when the flow was parked on its step's first wait, else the step re-runs); a step longer than settleMs is suspended before the turn is released; conversation timers run under the chat's turn; providers with capabilities.exclusiveSession (Baileys, Discord, Telegram polling) start only on the elected replica (on the others bot.send rejects ProviderNotLeaderError). Lost lease: sends reject LeaseLostError; no turn: CoordinationUnavailableError on 'error'. Events 'coordination:leader'|'coordination:follower'|'coordination:lease-lost'. Tests: MemoryCoordinator + MemoryCoordinationHub (crash() simulates a dead replica). Without coordination nothing changes.
- v1 sub-APIs (bot.groups/profile/privacy/chats/presence) were REMOVED — reach the Baileys socket via provider.socket for WhatsApp-specific ops

## @bot-wa/ai (separate package)
- Install (once published): pnpm add @bot-wa/ai + the chosen provider's SDK (@anthropic-ai/sdk, openai, or @google/generative-ai; ollama needs none, it talks plain HTTP via fetch; the 9 presets need only openai)
- bot.plug(aiPlugin({ provider, model, apiKey, baseUrl, persona, maxTokens, effort, thinking, timeoutMs, context: { maxMessages }, autoReply, resetCommand, errorMessage, refusalMessage, humanizeTyping })) — catch-all text autoresponder with per-chat history + a /reset command (install after slashCommandsPlugin so its /reset wins)
- Providers: 'anthropic' (default; default model claude-opus-4-8), 'openai' and 'ollama' (both require `model` explicitly), 'gemini' (default gemini-2.0-flash), and OpenAI-compatible presets 'deepseek'|'qwen'|'glm'|'kimi'|'groq'|'openrouter'|'mistral'|'grok'|'together' (each with its conventional env var, e.g. DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, and a default model)
- timeoutMs (default 60000) aborts a hung non-streaming call so it cannot block the chat queue
- ctx.tools.ai (AIClient, via bot.provide('ai', client)): ask(prompt), generate(input), stream(input)
- Tools: aiPlugin({ tools: { name: { description (model-only), title? (user-facing label), schema (JSON Schema validated: type/required/properties/enum/const/items/additionalProperties:false/minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength/minItems/maxItems, or safeParse), handler(args, tctx), confirm?, confirmMessage?, labels? ({ argKey: { value: 'Human label' } }, shown in the default confirmation), confirmLines?: (args) => string[] (e.g. code-computed prices/total), dedupe?: 'args' | { windowMs }, timeoutMs? } }, toolConfirm: { yes?, no?, timeout?, buttons?, answeredNotice?, expiredNotice?, systemNote? } }). On channels with native buttons (capabilities.buttons: Telegram, Cloud API, Discord, Messenger, Instagram) the confirmation is a Yes/No buttons message (ai.tools.button.yes/no, prompt ai.tools.confirmButtons without the (sí/no) hint); a press equals typing yes/no (typing still works), is acknowledged, buttons are removed by edit where supported (Telegram, Discord), stale presses are acknowledged and dropped before routing (where buttons cannot be edited away — Cloud API, Messenger, Instagram — they get a localized ai.tools.confirmExpired reply unless toolConfirm.expiredNotice: false; toolConfirm.answeredNotice: true also replies ai.tools.confirmAnswered on a press); confirmWith(c, { buttons?, ctx?, answeredNotice? }) inside your own conversation uses the same buttons (ctx from replyInChat's ctx); channels without buttons get the typed question; toolConfirm.buttons: false forces text. Arguments are validated BEFORE confirmation (use enum for product keys). confirm: true asks a readable prompt ("Voy a: Crear pedido\n• 5 × torta_chocolate\n¿Confirmas? (sí/no)"); a clear yes runs, a clear no denies, anything else (e.g. "sí pero cambia a 5") is NOT run and returns { executed: false, reason: 'user_replied', userReply } to the model. A system prompt note tells the model not to ask for confirmation itself. Successful confirm/dedupe runs are remembered per chat (repeat notice; dedupe returns { executed: false, reason: 'duplicate', previous }); a handler returning { error } is not remembered as done. Best practices for side-effecting tools: never let the model compute money (quote tool + totals computed in the handler and shown via confirmLines), enum-validate catalog values, provide update/cancel/list tools alongside create, dedupe on create, return { error } for unknown ids, keep confirm on side effects
- Formatting: the autoreply converts the model's Markdown per chat with ctx.textFormat = provider.textFormatFor?(chatId) ?? capabilities.textFormat ('whatsapp' → *bold* _italic_ ~strike~ •; 'plain' strips markers; 'markdown' unchanged; Twilio: whatsapp: chats 'whatsapp', SMS 'plain'); aiPlugin({ format: 'auto' | TextFormat | false }); formatMarkdown(text, format)
- Testing: MockAIProvider (implements AIProvider, no network) + ContextManager/AIClient exported for unit tests
- WhatsApp policy: since 2026-01-15 Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform terms prohibit general-purpose AI assistants (open-ended ChatGPT-style chatbots). AI that serves the business's own customers (support, sales, bookings) is allowed. Always write a persona scoped to one business that declines unrelated requests; do not generate "ask me anything" WhatsApp bots.
